grammar_rule.title: Broad & Slender Consonants
grammar_rule.explanation: In Irish, consonants can be broad or slender, affecting the pronunciation of nearby vowels. Broad consonants are pronounced with a wider mouth shape, while slender consonants are pronounced with a narrower mouth shape.

pronunciation_notes: Practice pronouncing broad and slender consonants to improve your Irish accent.
Pay attention to fada (accent marks) as they change the pronunciation of vowels.
